headline: Trump’s Push for Data Centers on Public Land Faces Top Senate Democrat’s Scrutiny
author: Ari Natter

paragraphs.text: Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:15 PM EST 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- A top Senate Democrat is putting the Trump administration's moves to build data centers on public land in the crosshairs, foreshadowing a brewing fight when his party takes control of Congress next year.

In a letter to the Bureau of Land Management, Senator Martin Heinrich said the agency is considering at least 15 proposals to build data centers on related infrastructure on public land covering more than 17,000 acres stretching across six Western states. That comes after the administration approved an 88-acre data center site in Boulder City, Nevada this past June, according to Heinrich, who is poised to become chair of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee next year.

"I am extremely concerned with the Trump administration's actions to develop data centers on public lands,"Heinrich wrote in the letter to Steve Pearce, the director of the Bureau of Land Management, which has jurisdiction over hundreds of millions of acres of public lands.

In his letter Heinrich requested the Bureau of Land Management provide a list of all the authorities being used, related development proposals and the potential sites that were earmarked for data center development on public lands.

An Interior Department spokesperson said any right of way application involving public lands follows the established National Environmental Policy Act process, which includes rigorous environmental review, opportunities for public input, and full transparency.

"The Department's focus continues to be ensuring that any proposed use of public lands is evaluated carefully, openly, and in a way that protects communities, natural resources, and the long-term interests of the American people," the spokesperson said in an email.

President Donald Trump signed an executive order in July 2025 seeking to expedite the permitting of data centers on public land saying the facilities were a priority for the administration's goals of manufacturing and technical dominance.
